doc.title: Sam Most interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999

title: Red Norvo, Frank Sinatra and the wooden flute
summary: With Red Norvo's group Sinatra gave him a handmade wooden flute at his Palm Springs house.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working with Sinatra: bands, Vegas and the Sands

blocks.x: How did this come about? A wooden flute?

Oh yeah, I wanted to tell you about that. I was with Red Norvo for a number of years. I went to Las Vegas, Tahoe. And so he used to go on the road with Frank Sinatra. In fact the record came out recently with Frank Sinatra with the Red Norvo group. So we were playing in Palm Springs and we went over to Frank’s house. I played piano for Frank. He sang “Lady is a Tramp.”

At the house in Palm Springs. And he used to come into The Sands in Vegas and also the place Rimrocks in Palm Springs. He’d come in sometimes and just pass the group going into the lounge and say, “Hey Sam you’re blowing your ass off” or something like that. Anyhow we were in Palm Springs and we played a little thing for him, and he came out with this thing and he said, “Sam, I want you to see something.” So he came out with this box and I opened it and it’s a flute, like a wooden flute made in Rudelcard, England, supposed to be hand made. And he said, “I know you’d appreciate it, it’s yours.” I flipped. You know Frank Sinatra giving me a beautiful flute. I couldn’t sleep. I says wow, he gave me a flute, you know, Frank Sinatra. And so that’s the flute in the picture. I was — Zan Stewart out here was doing an interview and he said, “We’ll take a picture for the magazine.” So that was the picture, and the guy who was taking the picture said well we’ll just change your shirt and maybe you can use some of these pictures. That’s what happened. Of course I hadn’t had any pictures for a while other than the one of the cover, you know the Xanadu cover.
